---
title: Prose citations
description: Link a prose answer to submitted tool results and check claims against authorized evidence.
---

Set `citations` in `Agent.create()` to check references in an ordinary prose
answer. This option is off by default. It works with the Node `anthropic()`
adapter's plain SDK requests, including successful streams. Typed output,
other adapters, thinking requests and requests carrying a signed replay prefix
are outside the feature's scope.

## Configure a citation check

Declare which tool, entity, field and executed arguments can establish a
claim. Provide a synchronous `authorizeEvidence` policy that separately
permits retention of the original structured result and the selected scope
arguments. Derive the claim's entity, value and intended scope from the prose
and your application context. Reading the intended scope from the cited result
would let that result choose the question it is judged against.

<CodeFile
  path="examples/features/125-prose-citations.ts"
  region="cite-prose"
  title="Check a measurement citation against its declared scope"
/>

The [runnable example](https://github.com/footprintjs/agentfootprint/blob/main/examples/features/125-prose-citations.ts)
uses a scripted SDK client and synthetic data. It needs no API key and makes
no network requests. In your app, use `anthropic()` with your usual
credentials and make the authorization decision for the current reader.

## Read the result

After the run, read `(await agent.assessment())?.citations`. An offered
marker links to a particular tool result body in the request that produced
the accepted response. The slot is meaningful within that offer. Submission
establishes which body the request contained. It cannot establish that the
model attended to that body.

- `supported` means the cited reading agrees with the authored claim for
  its entity, field and scope.
- `contradicted` means the comparable reading disagrees in that scope.
- `unverified` covers unresolved claims, incomplete scope or coverage and
  unavailable evidence. A finding with a slot can still identify the source
  even if the claim could not be checked. A copied marker from an earlier
  request can be unverified without a slot.

Citation findings describe the terminal prose. Existing output and input
policies keep their own retry, refusal and streaming behavior. The citation
checker uses deterministic comparisons and adds no model call.

## Compare two readings

Add `comparisonGroups: [{ concept, rules: [firstRuleId, secondRuleId] }]` for
independent tools with rules about the same concept. Use scope dimensions
named `unit` and `grain`, declare `periodDimension` with an absolute queried
interval, and include any other qualifiers. Values from two authorized tool
results are compared only when their entity, field and scope match, coverage
admits the queried period and the values have comparable types.

`citations.conflicts` contains pairs of offer slots. A pair can be reported
even if neither slot appears in a prose marker. `comparisonComplete`
describes the bounded comparison pass. An empty list can also mean no
comparable pair was available.

## Check a requested column

`requestedColumn` reads one explicit column name from the admitted user
message. `completeColumns` supplies the whole authorized visible column
set for the submitted result. When the answer cites one governing source,
the checker can report that the requested column is absent and suggest a
uniquely nearest visible name. Return `undefined` when visibility is partial
or the full column set is unknown.

## Evidence and privacy

Authorize retention only when both the original structured facts and the
selected scope can be retained. The citation assessment exposes the
structural verdict, prose position, offer slots and any authorized column
suggestion. Private evidence is used for comparison. The public assessment
omits retained source contents and internal proof identifiers. Apply your
existing content and recording policies to the prose and tool messages
themselves.
